name: main: all checks green
_comment: Repository ruleset, version-controlled so the merge policy is reviewable
as a diff rather than living only in a settings page nobody can audit.
Rulesets are repository-scoped: this applies to every push and every pull
request targeting the branches in `conditions`, on every branch, not to
one PR. Anything committed to the repo (workflows, JSON schemas, the
coverage gate in pyproject.toml, .claude hooks) is already repo-scoped
once it is on the default branch -- files do not need a ruleset to apply
everywhere. What needs one is BLOCKING: refusing a merge when a check is
not green. That is a GitHub setting, not a file, which is why this exists.
Underscore-prefixed keys are stripped before the payload is sent.

rules._why: The default branch must not be deletable.
No force-pushes to the default branch: they rewrite history other checkouts depend on.

_why: Changes reach the default branch through a pull request, so the checks
below actually run before merge.
required_approving_review_count is 0 because this is a single-maintainer
repository and a non-zero count would block every merge; raise it when
there is a second reviewer.
required_review_thread_resolution leaves no unresolved review thread
behind a merge.
These are the GATE checks, not the individual jobs. Requiring a job
directly reintroduces the hole this is meant to close: a job skipped by
an `if:`, or never reached because an earlier job failed, posts no check
at all, and a required check that never reports is satisfied by being
absent. Each gate depends on every job in its workflow and runs with
`if: always()`, so it reports on every run and fails on any non-success.
strict_required_status_checks_policy requires the branch to be up to
date with the base first: without it, a green result measured against
an older base can be merged into a base that has since changed.
'Cloud review gate (all jobs green)' is deliberately NOT required.
CLAUDE.md and docs/CLOUD_REVIEW.md both state the cloud review is
advisory and never approves or merges; requiring it would turn an
advisory bot into a merge blocker and would block on infrastructure
problems (a missing MONGODB_URI, an Atlas outage) that say nothing
about the change under review. Its gate job still runs, so its state is
always visible. Add the context here if that changes.
